title: Why open?
instructions: Why do you need to use the `open` keyword on a class in Kotlin before another class can inherit from it?

options.text: Kotlin requires open on every class
Kotlin classes are final by default, so open allows inheritance
open adds a constructor to the class

explanation: In Kotlin, all classes are final (closed) by default. This means no other class can inherit from them unless you mark them with the `open` keyword. This is a safety feature that prevents unintended inheritance.
